figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1 | β-Lactams are molecular mimics of the d-Ala–d-Ala terminal 
peptidoglycan motif. a, Penicillin-binding proteins normally recognize the 
terminal d-Ala–d-Ala motif and form an acyl-enzyme intermediate by insertion 
of a bond into d-Ala–d-Ala that eliminates the terminal d-Ala. The acyl-enzyme 
intermediate subsequently reacts with a second strand of peptidoglycan to 
form a cross-link, completing the catalytic cycle. b, Penicillin-binding proteins 
mistake penicillin for their natural substrate d-Ala–d-Ala, owing to molecular 
mimicry reacting with the lactam ring, and are thus unable to eliminate the 
terminal d-Ala (thiazole) motif, irreversibly blocking subsequent deacylation 
and catalytic turnover.
